title.zh: 卷429 列傳二百十六 江忠义 周宽世 石清吉 余际昌 林文察 赵德光 张文德
title.en: Volume 429 Biographies 216: Jiang Zhongyi, Zhou Kuanshi, Shi Qingji, Yu Jichang, Lin Wencha, Zhao Deguang, Zhang Wende
title.raw: 卷429 列傳二百十六 江忠义 周宽世 石清吉 余际昌 林文察 赵德光 张文德

sentences.zh: 列傳二百十六

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 216
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 216

sentences.zh: 江忠義週寬世石清吉餘際昌

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyi, Zhou Kuanshi, Shi Qingji, Yu Jichang
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyi, Zhou Kuanshi, Shi Qingji, and Yu Jichang

sentences.zh: 林文察趙德光張文德

translations.literal: Lin Wencha, Zhao Deguang, Zhang Wende
translations.idiomatic: Lin Wencha, Zhao Deguang, and Zhang Wende

sentences.zh: 江忠義，字味根，湖南新寧人，忠源從弟。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyi, courtesy name Weigen, was a native of Xinning in Hunan; he was a younger cousin of Jiang Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyi, styled Weigen, came from Xinning in Hunan and was a younger cousin of Jiang Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，忠源率楚勇援長沙，忠義年十八，從軍，轉戰湖北、江西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, Zhongyuan led Chu braves to relieve Changsha; Zhongyi was eighteen, joined the army, and fought in turn through Hubei and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852, when Zhongyuan led Hunan volunteers to the relief of Changsha, the eighteen-year-old Zhongyi took the field with him and campaigned through Hubei and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 忠源殉難廬州，遂分將其軍。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan died in battle at Luzhou, and he then took command of part of his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyuan fell at Luzhou, he took over part of the army.

sentences.zh: 五年，從提督和春复廬州，擢知縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he followed Grand Secretary He Chun in recovering Luzhou and was promoted to district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he served under Grand Secretary He Chun in the recovery of Luzhou and was promoted to district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 七年，劉長佑援江西，攻臨江不利，時忠義在籍，巡撫駱秉章檄率新練勇千人往助之，至則破石達開於平墟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Liu Changyou went to aid Jiangxi; the attack on Linjiang went badly. At that time Zhongyi was at home on leave; Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered him to lead a thousand newly trained braves to assist; on arrival he defeated Shi Dakai at Pingxu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857, when Liu Changyou's relief of Jiangxi stalled at Linjiang, Zhongyi was at home; Governor Luo Bingzhang summoned him with a thousand fresh recruits, and he routed Shi Dakai at Pingxu.

sentences.zh: 臨江既克，擢知府，賞花翎。

translations.literal: After Linjiang was taken, he was promoted to prefect and awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Linjiang fell, he was made prefect and given the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 八年，克崇仁，進攻新城，五戰皆捷，加道銜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he took Chongren, advanced to attack Xincheng, won five battles in succession, and was given the rank of circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he captured Chongren, pressed the attack on Xincheng, won five battles in a row, and received the rank of circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 江西肅清，凱歸。

translations.literal: Jiangxi was pacified, and he returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi was cleared, he marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開犯永州，忠義赴援，連戰破之，擢道員。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shi Dakai invaded Yongzhou; Zhongyi went to relieve it, defeated him in successive battles, and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, when Shi Dakai struck Yongzhou, Zhongyi hurried to its defense, beat him in a series of engagements, and was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊新寧摩訶嶺，扼武岡。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Mohe Ridge in Xinning and blocked Wugang.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels again at Mohe Ridge in Xinning and sealed off Wugang.

sentences.zh: 賊圍寶慶，忠義進援，會諸軍迭戰解圍，賜號額爾德木巴圖魯。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged Baoqing; Zhongyi advanced to relieve it; joining the armies in repeated battles, the siege was lifted, and he was granted the title Erde Muturu.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels besieged Baoqing, he marched to its relief; allied forces fought them off in a series of battles, and he was given the Mongol title Erde Muturu.

sentences.zh: 十年，駐守綏靖，母病歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he garrisoned Suijing; his mother fell ill and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he was posted to Suijing, but returned home when his mother fell ill.

sentences.zh: 賊遂陷綏寧、城步，圍武岡，忠義聞警，分軍守新寧，自援武岡，破其眾。

translations.literal: The rebels then took Suining and Chengbu and besieged Wugang; hearing the alarm, Zhongyi detached troops to hold Xinning and himself relieved Wugang, defeating their force.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then overran Suining and Chengbu and laid siege to Wugang. At the alarm Zhongyi left a detachment in Xinning and led the rest to Wugang, where he broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 新寧之賊走踞東安，一戰克之，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: The rebels from Xinning fled and occupied Dong'an; he took it in one battle and was given the rank of provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinning rebels fled into Dong'an; he seized the place in a single battle and was given the rank of provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又破賊於寧遠四廣橋。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Siguang Bridge in Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Siguang Bridge in Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，連破賊於全州白芒營、宜章栗源堡，還軍屯新寧，遣參將江忠朝扼全州，賊目餘成義斬其酋以降。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year, he defeated the rebels in succession at Baimang Camp in Quanzhou and Liyuan Fort in Yizhang, returned to encamp at Xinning, sent Brigadier Jiang Zhongchao to block Quanzhou, and the rebel officer Yu Chengyi beheaded his chief and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1861 he won successive victories at Baimang Camp in Quanzhou and Liyuan Fort in Yizhang, withdrew to Xinning, and sent Brigadier Jiang Zhongchao to hold Quanzhou, where the rebel officer Yu Chengyi killed his leader and submitted.

sentences.zh: 加二品頂戴，​​特擢署貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: He was given the second-rank official cap, and was specially promoted to act as governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received the second-rank cap and was specially appointed acting governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 石達開復自粵竄楚，眾號十萬，忠義以三千人扼會同，大破之。

translations.literal: Shi Dakai again raided from Guangdong into Hunan, his force said to number a hundred thousand; Zhongyi with three thousand men blocked him at Huitong and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai again swept from Guangdong into Hunan at the head of a force said to number a hundred thousand, Zhongyi met him at Huitong with three thousand men and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 賊糾湖北來鳳賊黨肆擾，擊走之，遂克來鳳。

translations.literal: The rebels rallied bandits from Laifeng in Hubei to raid widely; he drove them off and then took Laifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He drove off rebel allies from Laifeng in Hubei who had been raiding the countryside, then captured Laifeng itself.

sentences.zh: 達開走入四川。

translations.literal: Dakai fled into Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dakai withdrew into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丁母憂，請終制，詔允開署缺，仍在湖南勦賊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he entered mourning for his mother and asked to observe the full term; the edict permitted him to leave his acting post open and still suppress rebels in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he went into mourning for his mother and asked to complete the full period of filial leave; the court allowed him to keep his acting post vacant while he continued to fight rebels in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，移師援黔，克天柱，改授貴州提督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he moved his army to aid Guizhou, took Tianzhu, and was transferred to be provincial military commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he marched into Guizhou, captured Tianzhu, and was appointed provincial military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 調援廣西，克修仁，殪賊渠張高友。

translations.literal: He was transferred to aid Guangxi, took Xiuren, and killed the rebel leader Zhang Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangxi, he took Xiuren and killed the rebel chieftain Zhang Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 皖南賊熾，曾國籓疏調援皖，廣西巡撫劉長佑請留不遣，命署廣西提督。

translations.literal: Rebels in southern Anhui were fierce; Zeng Guofan memorialized to transfer him to aid Anhui; Guangxi Governor Liu Changyou asked to retain him and not send him away; he was ordered to act as provincial military commander of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels flared in southern Anhui, Zeng Guofan asked for him; Liu Changyou, governor of Guangxi, pleaded to keep him, and he was ordered to serve as acting provincial military commander of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二年，江西、廣東皆調援，先後報可，忠義以廣東兵有餘糧，他將足辦賊；

translations.literal: In the second year, both Jiangxi and Guangdong requested his aid, and approval was given in succession; Zhongyi held that Guangdong's troops had surplus grain and other generals were sufficient to handle the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 both Jiangxi and Guangdong sought his help, and each request was approved in turn; Zhongyi argued that Guangdong had ample supplies and other commanders enough to deal with the rebels there;

sentences.zh: 江西餉絀兵單，賊數十萬，萬一不支，東南全局瓦解，乃奏請力援江西。

translations.literal: Jiangxi had short rations and few troops, with rebels numbering hundreds of thousands; if it should not hold, the whole southeast would collapse; he therefore memorialized to throw his strength into aiding Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Jiangxi was short of pay and men while facing rebels said to number in the hundreds of thousands—if it gave way, the whole southeast would unravel—and he therefore asked leave to throw his full weight into Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 檄道員席寶田率前部先發，會剿陶家渡，自將攻湖口，逼賊營，屢出奇兵抄擊，斷文橋，攻太平關，賊酋黃文金受重創遁去，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He ordered Circuit Intendant Xi Baotian to lead the vanguard out first; they joined in suppressing Taojia Ford; he personally commanded the attack on Hukou, pressed the rebel camps, repeatedly sent surprise forces to strike from the flank, cut Wen Bridge, attacked Taiping Pass; the rebel chief Huang Wenjin was heavily wounded and fled; he was granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Circuit Intendant Xi Baotian ahead with the vanguard to join the action at Taojia Ford, then led the main body against Hukou, harrying the rebel camps with repeated flanking strikes, severing Wen Bridge and storming Taiping Pass until the rebel chief Huang Wenjin was badly wounded and fled; for this he received the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 進援青陽，分三路進戰，破賊壘，圍解，太平、石埭、寧國諸城賊第出降，詔嘉獎，予優敘。

translations.literal: He advanced to relieve Qingyang, attacked in three columns, broke the rebel forts, and lifted the siege; in Taiping, Shidi, Ningguo, and other cities the rebels came out to surrender rank by rank; an edict praised him and granted preferential recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Moving to relieve Qingyang, he attacked in three columns, stormed the rebel forts, and raised the siege; rebels in Taiping, Shidi, Ningguo, and neighboring towns surrendered in succession, and the court commended him with preferential honors.

sentences.zh: 會疾作，返就醫南昌，未至，卒於吳城，年甫三十。

translations.literal: He fell ill; returning to seek medical treatment at Nanchang, before he arrived he died at Wucheng, aged only thirty.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the march; bound for medical care at Nanchang, he died at Wucheng before he arrived, aged only thirty.

sentences.zh: 優詔悼惜，依總督例賜卹，贈尚書銜，諡誠恪，立功地建專祠。

translations.literal: A gracious edict mourned and lamented him; condolence was granted according to the precedent for governors-general; he was posthumously given the rank of minister of state, given the posthumous name Chenke, and a special shrine was built at the place of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned his loss, granted condolence on the scale reserved for governors-general, posthumously gave him ministerial rank and the posthumous name Chenke, and ordered a shrine built where he had won his fame.

sentences.zh: 光緒十一年，加贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Guangxu, he was further posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he was further posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從弟忠珀，記名提督。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Zhongpo was a provincial military commander on the register.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Zhongpo held the rank of provincial military commander on the register.

sentences.zh: 同治八年，剿貴州苗，攻克鎮遠、府衛二城，中砲亡，諡武愍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tongzhi, suppressing the Miao in Guizhou, he took the two cities Zhenyuan and Fuwei, was struck by artillery and died, and was given the posthumous name Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869, campaigning against the Miao in Guizhou, he captured Zhenyuan and Fuwei but was killed by artillery; he was posthumously named Wumin.

sentences.zh: 週寬世，字厚齋，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhou Kuanshi, courtesy name Houzhai, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kuanshi, styled Houzhai, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從湘軍，隸李續賓部下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he joined the Hunan Army and served under Li Xubin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he joined the Hunan Army and served under Li Xubin.

sentences.zh: 戰城陵磯、花園、半壁山，皆有功，擢千總。

translations.literal: He fought at Chenglingji, Huayuan, and Banbishan, distinguishing himself in each, and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself at Chenglingji, Huayuan, and Banbishan and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 從援江西，攻廣信，戰烏石山，寬世出左路突陣，為諸軍先，復其城，擢守備。

translations.literal: He followed the relief of Jiangxi, attacked Guangxin, fought at Wushi Mountain; Kuanshi led the left wing in a charge, was first among the armies, recovered the city, and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiangxi campaign he fought at Wushi Mountain during the assault on Guangxin; Kuanshi led the left wing in the charge, was first into the field, recovered the city, and was made garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 破賊義寧，擢都司。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels at Yining and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels at Yining and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 回援武漢，戰通城，寬世馳斬馬賊三，生擒七，以游擊補用。

translations.literal: Returning to relieve Wuhan, he fought at Tongcheng; Kuanshi charged and cut down three mounted rebels, took seven alive, and was appointed acting regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the march to relieve Wuhan he fought at Tongcheng, where Kuanshi charged down three mounted rebels and took seven prisoners, earning appointment as acting regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 從攻武昌，六年，李續賓夜出偵賊，之雙鳳山，突戰，寬世潛繞山趾橫擊之，賊敗奔；

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Wuchang; in the sixth year Li Xubin went out by night to reconnoiter the rebels, went to Shuangfeng Mountain, and joined battle suddenly; Kuanshi secretly circled the foot of the mountain and struck them across; the rebels were defeated and fled;
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Wuchang, in 1856 Li Xubin went out one night to scout Shuangfeng Mountain and was drawn into a sudden fight; Kuanshi slipped around the mountain's base and hit the rebels in the flank, sending them fleeing;

sentences.zh: 又戰鷹嘴，受砲傷，假歸。

translations.literal: he fought again at Eagle Beak, was wounded by artillery, and went home on leave.
translations.idiomatic: at Eagle Beak he was wounded by gunfire and went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 累功擢參將，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was promoted to brigadier and given the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated merit won him promotion to brigadier and the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 既而羅澤南卒於軍，續賓代將，召寬世回營。

translations.literal: Soon after Luo Zinan died in the army, Xubin took command in his place and summoned Kuanshi back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Zinan died in the field, Xubin succeeded to command and recalled Kuanshi to camp.

sentences.zh: 迭破賊於雙鳳山、魯家港、小龜山，克武漢，復大冶、興國，擢副將。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels in succession at Shuangfeng Mountain, Lujia Harbor, and Little Tortoise Hill, took Wuchang, recovered Daye and Xingguo, and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebels in turn at Shuangfeng Mountain, Lujia Harbor, and Little Tortoise Hill, captured Wuchang, recovered Daye and Xingguo, and was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 七年，從攻九江，破援賊於童司簰，毀其壘，賜號義勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the attack on Jiujiang, defeated relief rebels at Tongsi Pai, destroyed their forts, and was granted the title Yiyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857, during the siege of Jiujiang, he routed rebel reinforcements at Tongsi Pai, destroyed their forts, and received the title Yiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 破小池口賊屯，會克湖口，复彭澤。

translations.literal: He broke the rebel stockade at Xiaochikou, joined in taking Hukou, and recovered Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the rebel camp at Xiaochikou, helped take Hukou, and recovered Pengze.

sentences.zh: 賊由臨江犯興國，寬世率千六百人擊走之。

translations.literal: Rebels from Linjiang invaded Xingguo; Kuanshi with sixteen hundred men drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels from Linjiang struck Xingguo, Kuanshi with sixteen hundred men beat them back.

sentences.zh: 八年，回援湖北，戰麻城西南斗坡山。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned to aid Hubei and fought at Doupo Mountain southwest of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he returned to Hubei and fought at Doupo Mountain southwest of Macheng.

sentences.zh: 賊設伏，以馬隊誘戰，寬世待其近，突擊之，遂破其伏軍，進克黃安，而麻城亦下。

translations.literal: The rebels set an ambush and used cavalry to lure him into battle; Kuanshi waited until they were near and struck suddenly, thus breaking their ambush force, advanced and took Huang'an, and Macheng also fell.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels laid an ambush and sent cavalry to draw him on; Kuanshi held his men until they were close, then charged, broke the ambush, took Huang'an, and Macheng fell as well.

sentences.zh: 大軍克九江，論功，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: The main army took Jiujiang; in reckoning merit he was placed on the register as provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army captured Jiujiang, his merit earned him a place on the register as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 從李續賓進軍安徽，戰楓香鋪、小池驛，克太湖、潛山，搗舒城，寬世皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He followed Li Xubin in advancing into Anhui, fought at Fengxiangpu and Xiaochi Post, took Taihu and Qianshan, and raided Shucheng; Kuanshi was the army's vanguard in each.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Li Xubin into Anhui, fighting at Fengxiangpu and Xiaochi Post, capturing Taihu and Qianshan, and raiding Shucheng, with Kuanshi leading the van throughout.

sentences.zh: 十月，進攻三河，續賓戰沒，寬世斂餘眾守二日，彈丸俱盡，夜率親卒突圍，受重傷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they advanced to attack Sanhe; Xubin died in battle; Kuanshi gathered the survivors and held for two days until ammunition was exhausted; by night he led his personal troops in a breakout and was severely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, during the assault on Sanhe, Xubin was killed; Kuanshi rallied the survivors, held out two days until their ammunition was gone, then broke out by night at the head of his personal guard and was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，授湖南永州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed commander of the Yongzhou garrison in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開犯湖南，巡撫駱秉章令寬世募新軍二千援祁陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Shi Dakai invaded Hunan; Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Kuanshi to raise two thousand men of a new army to relieve Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859, when Shi Dakai invaded Hunan, Governor Luo Bingzhang ordered Kuanshi to raise two thousand fresh troops for the relief of Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 破賊長慶橋，又敗之長葉嶺。

translations.literal: He defeated the rebels at Changqing Bridge and again at Changye Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: He routed them at Changqing Bridge and again at Changye Ridge.

sentences.zh: 進援寶慶，屯城東，連敗賊長衝口、五里牌。

translations.literal: He advanced to relieve Baoqing, encamped east of the city, and defeated the rebels in succession at Changchongkou and Wulipai.
translations.idiomatic: Marching to relieve Baoqing, he encamped east of the city and won successive victories at Changchongkou and Wulipai.

sentences.zh: 李續宜援師至，會諸軍內外夾擊，賊解圍走。

translations.literal: Li Xuyi's relief force arrived; joining the armies in attack from within and without, the rebels lifted the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xuyi's relief column arrived, the allied forces struck from inside and outside the lines, and the rebels broke the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 回剿永州土匪，平之。

translations.literal: He returned to suppress bandits in Yongzhou and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Yongzhou, suppressed the local bandits, and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢湖南提督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he was made provincial military commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，赴安徽助剿，駐守桐城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he went to Anhui to assist in suppression and garrisoned Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he went to Anhui to join the campaign and garrisoned Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 二年，捻匪馬融和犯桐城，擊走之，移防六安。

translations.literal: In the second year the Nian bandit Ma Ronghe invaded Tongcheng; he drove them off and shifted defense to Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863, when the Nian leader Ma Ronghe struck Tongcheng, he beat them back and moved his garrison to Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 皖北漸定，調守安慶。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui was gradually pacified, and he was transferred to guard Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: As northern Anhui quieted, he was transferred to guard Anqing.

sentences.zh: 三年，赴援江西，克東鄉。

translations.literal: In the third year he went to aid Jiangxi and took Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he marched to Jiangxi's aid and captured Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 四年，破霆軍叛勇，追賊入廣東，會諸軍殲賊於嘉應。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he defeated mutinous braves of the Ting Army, pursued the rebels into Guangdong, and joined the armies in annihilating them at Jiaying.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 he crushed mutineers from the Ting Army, pursued the rebels into Guangdong, and with the allied forces destroyed them at Jiaying.

sentences.zh: 五年，回湖南提督任。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he returned to his post as provincial military commander of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he resumed his post as provincial military commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 傷發，乞休。

translations.literal: His wounds reopened and he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When his old wounds reopened, he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1887.

sentences.zh: 石清吉，字祥瑞，直隸沙河人。

translations.literal: Shi Qingji, courtesy name Xiangrui, was a native of Shahe in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qingji, styled Xiangrui, came from Shahe in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年武進士，官三等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang he passed the military jinshi examination and served as a third-rank imperial bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: A military jinshi of 1841, he served as a third-rank imperial bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，出為湖北鄖陽鎮守備，從剿黃陂、崇陽、應城，累擢參將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he went out as garrison commander of Yunyang in Hubei, followed in suppressing Huangpi, Chongyang, and Yingcheng, and was repeatedly promoted to brigadier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he was posted as garrison commander at Yunyang in Hubei, campaigned at Huangpi, Chongyang, and Yingcheng, and rose step by step to brigadier.

sentences.zh: 克安陸、京山皆有功，以勇稱，所統曰飛虎軍。

translations.literal: He distinguished himself in taking Anlu and Jingshan, was famed for valor, and his command was called the Flying Tiger Army.
translations.idiomatic: He won credit in the capture of Anlu and Jingshan, earned a reputation for valor, and commanded a force known as the Flying Tiger Army.

sentences.zh: 尋隸將軍都興阿軍，常從多隆阿轉戰。

translations.literal: Soon after he was attached to the army of General Duxing'a and often followed Duolong'a in campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon attached to General Duxing'a's command and campaigned repeatedly under Duolong'a.

sentences.zh: 七年，援蘄州，拔太湖，攻安慶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he relieved Qizhou, took Taihu, and attacked Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he relieved Qizhou, captured Taihu, and joined the attack on Anqing.

sentences.zh: 八年，由安慶退保宿松，大戰破賊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he withdrew from Anqing to defend Susong, fought a great battle, and defeated the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858, falling back from Anqing to Susong, he fought a major battle and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 九年，攻太湖。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he attacked Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he attacked Taihu.

sentences.zh: 十年，大戰小池，克太湖，功皆最。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he fought a great battle at Xiaochi, took Taihu, and his merit was foremost in each.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he fought a major battle at Xiaochi, captured Taihu, and ranked first in merit throughout.

sentences.zh: 十一年，安慶既下，會諸軍克桐城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, after Anqing had fallen, he joined the armies in taking Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, after Anqing fell, he joined the allied forces in the capture of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從攻廬州，清吉屯城西北，破賊壘，擒斬數千。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed the attack on Luzhou; Qingji encamped northwest of the city, broke rebel forts, and captured or killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862, during the siege of Luzhou, Qingji encamped northwest of the city, stormed the rebel forts, and killed or captured several thousand.

sentences.zh: 進毀賊柵，樹雲梯攻城，賊方死拒，而陳玉成兵敗遽去，遂由西門攻入，克廬州。

translations.literal: He advanced, destroyed rebel palisades, set scaling ladders against the wall to attack the city; the rebels were still resisting to the death when Chen Yucheng's army was defeated and suddenly withdrew; he then entered by the west gate and took Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed forward, tore down the palisades, and raised scaling ladders while the defenders fought to the last; then Chen Yucheng's army was routed and fled, and Qingji entered through the west gate and took Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 清吉累以戰功賜號幹勇巴圖魯，擢總兵，加提督銜。

translations.literal: For repeated battle merit Qingji was granted the title Ganyong Baturu, promoted to provincial military commander, and given the rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated victories Qingji received the title Ganyong Baturu, was made provincial military commander, and given provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿督師赴陝西，以清吉統五千人留守廬州。

translations.literal: Duolong'a led the army to Shaanxi and left Qingji in command of five thousand men to hold Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Duolong'a marched to Shaanxi, Qingji was left with five thousand men to hold Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，苗沛霖复叛，廬、壽、開土蜂匪起，清吉悉剿平之。

translations.literal: In the second year Miao Peilin rebelled again; bandits swarmed like bees in Lu, Shou, and Kai; Qingji suppressed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863, when Miao Peilin rebelled again and bandits swarmed through Lu, Shou, and Kai, Qingji stamped them out.

sentences.zh: 粵、捻諸匪合擾豫、楚之交，清吉赴援湖北，屯孝感、黃岡，拔難民近萬。

translations.literal: Guangdong and Nian bandits together harassed the border of Henan and Hubei; Qingji went to aid Hubei, encamped at Xiaogan and Huanggang, and rescued nearly ten thousand refugees.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong and Nian rebels together raided the Henan-Hubei border, Qingji marched to Hubei's aid, encamped at Xiaogan and Huanggang, and rescued nearly ten thousand civilians.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，匪酋陳得才、馬融和合犯蘄水，圍副都統富森保於關口。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year the bandit chiefs Chen Decai and Ma Ronghe jointly invaded Qishui and besieged Vice Commander Fusenbao at Guankou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of 1864 the bandit leaders Chen Decai and Ma Ronghe jointly attacked Qishui and besieged Vice Commander Fusenbao at Guankou.

sentences.zh: 清吉率軍馳援，會大霧，賊馬步數万麕集。

translations.literal: Qingji led his army in haste to relieve them; a great fog came up, and rebel cavalry and infantry numbering tens of thousands gathered in a swarm.
translations.idiomatic: Qingji hurried to the rescue; a thick fog descended, and tens of thousands of rebel horse and foot closed in around him.

sentences.zh: 清吉進至藥山，賊渡河抄後路，圍數重，截其四營為二。

translations.literal: Qingji advanced to Yaoshan; the rebels crossed the river to cut his rear; he was surrounded in many rings and his four camps were cut in two.
translations.idiomatic: At Yaoshan the rebels crossed the river behind him, wrapped him in ring after ring of encirclement, and cut his four camps in half.

sentences.zh: 自辰至午，血戰，被九創，殞於陣。

translations.literal: From the hour of chen to the hour of wu he fought a bloody battle, received nine wounds, and fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: From morning until noon he fought hand to hand, took nine wounds, and fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 從戰歿者，副將江星南、谷明發，游擊曾佔彪、段會元。

translations.literal: Those who died with him in battle were Deputy Commanders Jiang Xingnan and Gu Mingfa, and Regimental Commanders Zeng Zhanbiao and Duan Huiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commanders Jiang Xingnan and Gu Mingfa and regimental commanders Zeng Zhanbiao and Duan Huiyuan fell with him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔視提督陣亡例賜卹，入祀京師昭忠祠，予騎都尉世職，諡威毅，建專祠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict granted condolence according to the precedent for a provincial commander killed in battle, enshrined him in the Capital Shrine of Loyalty, gave a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, gave the posthumous name Weiyi, and built a special shrine.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him the honors due a provincial commander killed in battle, enshrined him in the Capital Shrine of Loyalty, gave his family a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, posthumously named him Weiyi, and ordered a shrine built in his memory.

sentences.zh: 餘際昌，湖北穀城人。

translations.literal: Yu Jichang was a native of Gucheng in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jichang came from Gucheng in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初入伍，剿匪積功至守備，署撫標右營游擊，為巡撫胡林翼所識拔。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he entered the army; through suppressing bandits he accumulated merit to garrison commander and acted as regimental commander of the governor's right battalion; he was recognized and promoted by Governor Hu Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted early in Xianfeng, rose through bandit suppression to garrison commander, served as acting regimental commander of the governor's right battalion, and won the patronage of Governor Hu Linyi.

sentences.zh: 七年，從戰黃梅、廣濟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in fighting at Huangmei and Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he fought at Huangmei and Guangji.

sentences.zh: 八年，陳玉成自太湖竄蘄州，際昌奉檄防皖、楚之交，敗賊南陽河，毀賊壘三十餘，擒賊目。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chen Yucheng fled from Taihu into Qizhou; Jichang received orders to defend the border of Anhui and Hubei, defeated the rebels at Nanyang River, destroyed more than thirty rebel forts, and captured a rebel officer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858, when Chen Yucheng broke out of Taihu toward Qizhou, Jichang was ordered to hold the Anhui-Hubei border; he routed the rebels at Nanyang River, destroyed more than thirty forts, and took a rebel officer prisoner.

sentences.zh: 賊走英山，追躡之，復其城，擢游擊。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Yingshan; he pursued and recovered the city, and was promoted to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them to Yingshan, recovered the city, and was promoted to regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 又破賊彌陀寺，晉參將。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Mituo Temple and was advanced to brigadier.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Mituo Temple and was advanced to brigadier.

sentences.zh: 李續賓軍覆三河，潛山、太湖复陷，際昌屯英山，遏潛、太之衝。

translations.literal: Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe; Qianshan and Taihu fell again; Jichang encamped at Yingshan and blocked the route between Qian and Tai.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xubin's army was destroyed at Sanhe and Qianshan and Taihu fell again, Jichang held Yingshan and blocked the corridor between Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 九年，進拔天堂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he advanced and took Tiantang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 he advanced and captured Tiantang.

sentences.zh: 賊大舉來爭，際昌敗諸王婆坳，追至雞冠嶺而還。

translations.literal: The rebels came in force to contest it; Jichang defeated them at Wangpo'ao, pursued to Jiguan Ridge, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came up in force to retake the ground; Jichang routed them at Wangpo'ao, pursued them to Jiguan Ridge, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 再敗賊槎水畈，斬馘千餘。

translations.literal: He again defeated the rebels at Chashui Fan and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Chashui Fan, killing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 時大軍圍太湖急，陳玉成糾黨十餘萬相持小池驛。

translations.literal: At that time the main army was pressing the siege of Taihu; Chen Yucheng mustered more than one hundred thousand followers and faced them at Xiaochi Post.
translations.idiomatic: While the main Qing force pressed the siege of Taihu, Chen Yucheng rallied more than a hundred thousand men and held them at bay at Xiaochi Post.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，際昌偕金國琛由間道出高橫嶺，與諸軍夾擊，大破之，遂復太湖，乘勝會攻克潛山，擢副將，署湖北督標中軍副將。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, Jichang together with Jin Guochen took a bypath over Mount Gaohheng, joined other armies in a converging attack, and inflicted a great defeat; he then recovered Taihu and, pressing the advantage, joined in capturing Qianshan; he was promoted to deputy commander and appointed acting deputy commander of the governor's central battalion in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1860, Jichang and Jin Guochen stole over Mount Gaohheng by a hidden route, struck the rebels with converging forces, and won a crushing victory; Taihu was recovered, Qianshan fell in the same advance, and Jichang was made deputy commander and acting deputy commander of the Hubei governor's central battalion.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成自六安回援安慶，霍山复陷。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng returned from Lu'an to relieve Anqing, and Huoshan fell again.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng turned back from Lu'an to relieve Anqing, and Huoshan was lost again.

sentences.zh: 際昌偕總兵成大吉擊破之，复霍山，加總兵銜。

translations.literal: Jichang together with provincial commander Cheng Daji defeated him, recovered Huoshan, and was given the rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang and provincial commander Cheng Daji routed him, retook Huoshan, and Jichang received provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 十一年，陳玉成入霍山，自黑石渡撲樂兒嶺。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Chen Yucheng entered Huoshan and, crossing from Heishi Ford, struck at Le'er Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, Chen Yucheng entered Huoshan and, crossing at Heishi Ford, drove at Le'er Ridge.

sentences.zh: 際昌軍潰，賊上竄黃州，革職留營。

translations.literal: Jichang's army was routed; the rebels fled upward into Huangzhou; he was dismissed from office but kept with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jichang's force was broken, the rebels fled up into Huangzhou, and he was stripped of rank but kept on with the camp.

sentences.zh: 尋從克黃州，率新募昌勝五營援河南。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed in the capture of Huangzhou and led the five newly recruited Changsheng battalions to aid Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took part in the recovery of Huangzhou, then led five newly raised Changsheng battalions to aid Henan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，屯陳留。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he encamped at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he encamped at Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 捻匪麕集杞縣，際昌馳擊，大破之，進拔焦、趙二寨，復原官，賜號偉勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Nian bandits gathered thickly at Qixian; Jichang galloped to attack and inflicted a great defeat; he advanced to take the two stockades of Jiao and Zhao, was restored to his original office, and was granted the title Weiyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian bandits massed at Qixian, Jichang rode out, smashed them, and took the Jiao and Zhao stockades; his former rank was restored and he received the title Weiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十月，攻捻於汝寧，破平輿寨，生擒賊酋陳文，詔以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he attacked the Nian at Runing, broke Pingyu Stockade, captured the rebel chieftain Chen Wen alive, and was ordered to be recorded as provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he fought the Nian at Runing, stormed Pingyu Stockade, took the rebel chief Chen Wen alive, and was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁嘉其勇，令充翼長，從剿渦河，斬賊渠楊興太等。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen praised his bravery, appointing him wing commander; he followed in suppressing the Guo River rebels and beheaded the rebel ringleaders Yang Xingtai and others.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen commended his courage, made him a wing commander, and sent him against the Guo River bandits, where he cut down the ringleader Yang Xingtai and others.

sentences.zh: 二年春，追破陳大喜於阜陽吳老莊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he pursued and defeated Chen Daxi at Wulaozhuang in Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1863 he pursued and defeated Chen Daxi at Wulaozhuang in Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 捻首張總愚竄侯集，際昌會張曜夜襲之，擒其黨獨角虎、週馬，授河北鎮總兵。

translations.literal: The Nian chief Zhang Zongyu fled to Houji; Jichang joined Zhang Yao in a night raid, captured his followers Dujiaohu and Zhou Ma, and was appointed provincial commander of Hebei garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chief Zhang Zongyu slipped into Houji, Jichang and Zhang Yao raided the camp by night, seized his lieutenants Dujiaohu and Zhou Ma, and Jichang was made provincial commander of the Hebei garrison.

sentences.zh: 夏，逐賊楚、豫間，敗之麻城，躡至方家寨，中伏力戰，受三十餘創，死之。

translations.literal: In summer he pursued rebels between Chu and Yu, defeated them at Macheng, tracked them to Fangjia Stockade, fell into an ambush and fought fiercely, received more than thirty wounds, and died.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he chased rebels across the Hubei-Henan border, routed them at Macheng, and followed them to Fangjia Stockade, where he walked into an ambush, fought on through more than thirty wounds, and fell.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉世職，諡威毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made provincial commander, given a hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, and posthumously named Weiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to provincial commander, his family received a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous name Weiyi.

sentences.zh: 林文察，字子明，福建台灣人。

translations.literal: Lin Wencha, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Taiwan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Wencha, styled Ziming, came from Taiwan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 咸豐八年，從剿台灣淡水土匪，捐餉助軍，以游擊留福建補用。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xianfeng he followed in suppressing Tamsui bandits in Taiwan, donated funds to aid the army, and was retained in Fujian for assignment as regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he helped suppress Tamsui bandits in Taiwan, donated supplies to the army, and was kept in Fujian for appointment as regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，九壟山匪郭萬淙掠建寧、邵武間，汀州、龍嚴匪胡熊擾寧洋、永安。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Jiulong Mountain bandit Guo Wancong raided between Jianning and Shaowu, while the Tingzhou and Longyan bandit Hu Xiong harassed Ningyang and Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 the Jiulong Mountain bandit Guo Wancong raided between Jianning and Shaowu, and the Tingzhou and Longyan bandit Hu Xiong troubled Ningyang and Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 文察隨軍進剿，擒其黨百餘人。

translations.literal: Wencha followed the army in the campaign and captured more than a hundred of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Wencha marched with the punitive force and took more than a hundred of their followers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 郭萬淙遁據邵武上山坊，文察合軍蹙之，降其眾，复破胡熊於東板土寨，擒之，擢參將，賜號固勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Guo Wancong fled and held Shangshanfang in Shaowu; Wencha combined armies to press him and accepted the surrender of his followers; he again defeated Hu Xiong at Dongban Tuzhai, captured him, was promoted to brigadier, and was granted the title Guyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wancong fled to Shangshanfang in Shaowu; Wencha closed in with united forces and accepted the mass surrender, then broke Hu Xiong at Dongban Tuzhai and took him alive; Wencha was made brigadier and given the title Guyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，援浙，克江山，晉副將，晉號烏訥思齊巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went to aid Zhejiang, captured Jiangshan, was advanced to deputy commander, and advanced in title to Uneesiqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he went to aid Zhejiang, captured Jiangshan, was promoted to deputy commander, and received the advanced title Uneesiqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 汀州、連城相繼陷，文察回援，破賊金雞嶺，設伏，敗之江防，遂拔連城，乘勝克汀州，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Tingzhou and Liancheng fell in succession; Wencha returned to their relief, defeated the rebels at Jinji Ridge, set an ambush and defeated them at the river defense line, then took Liancheng and, pressing the victory, captured Tingzhou; he was recorded as provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhou and Liancheng fell in turn, Wencha hurried back, routed the rebels at Jinji Ridge, ambushed them along the river line, retook Liancheng, and pressed on to capture Tingzhou; he was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 冬，杭州既陷，調援浙，文察領台勇二千人駐衢州。

translations.literal: In winter, after Hangzhou had fallen, he was transferred to aid Zhejiang; Wencha led two thousand Taiwan braves and encamped at Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after Hangzhou fell, he was sent again to Zhejiang with two thousand Taiwan braves and stationed at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，破處州賊屯，而遂昌陷，文察進軍逼之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he broke the rebel strongholds at Chuzhou, but Suichang fell; Wencha advanced his army to press them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 he smashed the rebel camps at Chuzhou, but Suichang then fell, and Wencha marched in to press the enemy.

sentences.zh: 李世賢自江山來援，文察設伏大柘、大廟及石練山之前後，賊至，擊走之。

translations.literal: Li Shixian came from Jiangshan to their relief; Wencha set ambushes before and behind Dazhe, Damiao, and Mount Shilian; when the rebels arrived he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixian marched from Jiangshan to relieve them, but Wencha had laid ambushes around Dazhe, Damiao, and Mount Shilian and drove the rebels back when they arrived.

sentences.zh: 夜，賊來劫營，復為伏兵所敗，复遂昌，進克松陽。

translations.literal: At night the rebels came to raid the camp and were again defeated by ambush troops; he recovered Suichang and advanced to take Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebels tried to storm the camp and were beaten again by the ambush force; Wencha retook Suichang and went on to capture Songyang.

sentences.zh: 會總兵秦如虎攻處州，賊棄城遁，並克縉雲，授福寧鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When provincial commander Qin Ruhu attacked Chuzhou the rebels abandoned the city and fled; Jinyun was also taken, and Wencha was appointed provincial commander of Funing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When provincial commander Qin Ruhu attacked Chuzhou the rebels abandoned the city; Jinyun fell as well, and Wencha was appointed provincial commander of the Funing garrison.

sentences.zh: 尋擢福建提督。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to provincial commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to provincial commander of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二年，台灣不靖，總督左宗棠令渡台號召舊部，統領諸軍。

translations.literal: In the second year Taiwan was unsettled; Governor-General Zuo Zongtang ordered him to cross the strait and summon his old followers to command all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863, when Taiwan was in turmoil, Governor-General Zuo Zongtang ordered him to cross the strait, rally his old troops, and take command of the field armies.

sentences.zh: 文察分軍攻彰化及鬥六，克之。

translations.literal: Wencha divided his army to attack Changhua and Douliu and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Wencha split his force, attacked Changhua and Douliu, and took both.

sentences.zh: 諭降諸莊，賊渠戴萬生、林戇晟遁走。

translations.literal: He persuaded various villages to surrender; the rebel ringleaders Dai Wansheng and Lin Gansheng fled.
translations.idiomatic: He induced many villages to submit, while the rebel chiefs Dai Wansheng and Lin Gansheng fled.

sentences.zh: 三年，破樵溪口賊莊，斬其酋林傳，毀張厝莊、四塊厝賊巢，戴萬生、林戇晟並伏誅。

translations.literal: In the third year he broke the rebel village at Qiaoxikou, beheaded its chieftain Lin Chuan, destroyed the rebel nests at Zhangcuo Village and Sikuaicuo, and Dai Wansheng and Lin Gansheng were both executed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he stormed the rebel village at Qiaoxikou, killed its chief Lin Chuan, destroyed the nests at Zhangcuo Village and Sikuaicuo, and Dai Wansheng and Lin Gansheng were both put to death.

sentences.zh: 粵匪李世賢、汪海洋合陷漳州，文察倉猝率二百人內渡，遇賊萬松關，歿於陣，贈太子少保，予騎都尉世職，諡剛愍。

translations.literal: Guangdong rebels Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang together took Zhangzhou; Wencha in haste led two hundred men back across the strait, met rebels at Wansong Pass, and died in battle; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and posthumously named Gangmin.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang together seized Zhangzhou, Wencha hurried back across the strait with only two hundred men, met the enemy at Wansong Pass, and fell in battle; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, his family received a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and he was given the posthumous name Gangmin.

sentences.zh: 本籍及漳州建專祠。

translations.literal: Special shrines were built in his native place and at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines were erected in his native district and at Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子朝棟，光緒中，法兵犯台灣，陷基隆，朝棟率家兵助戰有功，捐鉅貲，賜四品京堂，有聲於時。

translations.literal: His son Chaodong, in the Guangxu period when French troops invaded Taiwan and took Keelung, led household troops to aid the fighting with merit, donated a large sum, was granted Fourth Rank Capital Official, and was renowned in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chaodong, during the Guangxu reign when French forces invaded Taiwan and took Keelung, led family troops into the fight with distinction, gave a large donation, received the rank of Fourth Rank Capital Official, and won a wide reputation.

sentences.zh: 趙德光，原姓張，貴州郎岱人。

translations.literal: Zhao Deguang, original surname Zhang, was a native of Langdai in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Deguang, whose original surname was Zhang, came from Langdai in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 從副將趙德昌轉戰雲南，德昌弟畜之，故冒姓趙氏。

translations.literal: He followed deputy commander Zhao Dechang in campaigns through Yunnan; Dechang's younger brother raised him, so he falsely took the surname Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned through Yunnan under deputy commander Zhao Dechang, was raised by Dechang's younger brother, and therefore bore the Zhao surname in name only.

sentences.zh: 拔補千總，擢都司。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed company commander, then promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected for company command and later promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，自領一軍，戰獨山，屢敗賊，擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng he personally commanded an army, fought at Dushan, repeatedly defeated rebels, and was promoted to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he took command of his own force, fought at Dushan, repeatedly routed the rebels, and was made regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊窺省城，德光擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year rebels watched for a chance against the provincial capital; Deguang drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861, when rebels probed the provincial capital, Deguang beat them back.

sentences.zh: 又敗之羊場平寨，設伏於主戎山麓，殪賊無算，擢參將，賜號豪勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He again defeated them at Yangchangping Stockade, set an ambush at the foot of Mount Zhurong, and killed rebels beyond count; he was promoted to brigadier and granted the title Haoyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated them again at Yangchangping Stockade, laid an ambush at the foot of Mount Zhurong, and cut down rebels beyond counting; he was made brigadier and given the title Haoyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 教匪踞玉華、尚大坪，以王卡為屏蔽。

translations.literal: Teaching-cult rebels held Yuhua and Shangdaping, with Wangka as their shield.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching-cult rebels held Yuhua and Shangdaping, using Wangka as their cover.

sentences.zh: 德光率所部攻破楊義司、郭家莊、馬籠口賊營，斷其援，又破腰蘿溪、新砦岩要隘，進偪王卡。

translations.literal: Deguang led his detachments to break the rebel camps at Yangyisi, Guojiazhuang, and Malongkou, cutting off their relief; he again broke the vital passes at Yaoluoxi and Xinzhaiyan and advanced to press Wangka.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang led his troops in storming the rebel camps at Yangyisi, Guojiazhuang, and Malongkou, severed their relief lines, then broke the passes at Yaoluoxi and Xinzhaiyan and closed on Wangka.

sentences.zh: 德光先登，賊大潰，救出男婦數千人，擢副將。

translations.literal: Deguang was first to ascend; the rebels broke in great disorder; he rescued several thousand men and women and was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang was the first over the wall; the rebels collapsed, and he freed several thousand captive men and women before being promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，壩芒匪首潘明杰由龍里窺伺省城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, the Baman bandit chieftain Pan Mingjie from Longli watched for a chance against the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 the Baman bandit chief Pan Mingjie moved from Longli to probe the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 德光迎擊三江橋，賊敗走。

translations.literal: Deguang met them at Sanjiang Bridge and the rebels were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang met them at Sanjiang Bridge and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 進攻甲秀閣賊巢，遂克龍里舊縣，補都勻協副將，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack the rebel nest at Jiaxiu Pavilion, then took the old Longli district; he was appointed deputy commander of the Duyun garrison and recorded as provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on the rebel stronghold at Jiaxiu Pavilion, recovered old Longli district, was appointed deputy commander of the Duyun garrison, and was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 三年，尚大坪匪撲省城，德光與布政使龔自閎等固守，賊尋退，加提督銜，署古州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the third year Shangdaping rebels struck the provincial capital; Deguang together with Administration Commissioner Gong Zihong and others held firm; the rebels soon withdrew; he was given the rank of provincial commander and appointed acting provincial commander of Guzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, when Shangdaping rebels assaulted the provincial capital, Deguang and Administration Commissioner Gong Zihong held the city until the enemy withdrew; he received provincial commander rank and served as acting commander of the Guzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 旋解清鎮圍，克龍里、廣順、定番、長寨，以提督記名。

translations.literal: He then lifted the siege of Qingzhen, took Longli, Guangshun, Dingfan, and Changzhai, and was recorded as provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: He soon relieved Qingzhen, captured Longli, Guangshun, Dingfan, and Changzhai, and was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 四年，匪首何二久踞開州、尚大坪，擾近省州縣，無寧歲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the bandit chieftain He Erjiu held Kaizhou and Shangdaping, harassing the nearby prefectures and districts year after year without peace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 the bandit chief He Erjiu held Kaizhou and Shangdaping and kept the neighboring prefectures in turmoil year after year.

sentences.zh: 德光選精銳過清水江剿之。

translations.literal: Deguang selected elite troops and crossed the Qingshui River to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang picked elite troops and crossed the Qingshui River to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 賊糾集苗匪、教匪沿江以拒，乘間過江攻開州。

translations.literal: The rebels gathered Miao bandits and teaching-cult rebels along the river to resist, and seizing an opening crossed the river to attack Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rallied Miao and teaching-cult bandits along the river to block him, then slipped across and struck Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 德光固守十餘日，殺賊八九百人，乘勝追擊，克沿江獅子坉、鎮江坉、三龍營賊屯。

translations.literal: Deguang held firm for more than ten days, killing eight or nine hundred rebels; pressing the victory in pursuit he took the rebel strongholds of Shizidian, Zhenjiangdian, and Sanlongying along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang held out for more than ten days, killed eight or nine hundred rebels, then pursued them and captured the river strongholds at Shizidian, Zhenjiangdian, and Sanlongying.

sentences.zh: 進克濱江賊巢，斬馘二千餘，何二棄尚大坪而遁，被優敘，署安義鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He advanced to take the rebel nest on the riverbank, beheading more than two thousand; He Er abandoned Shangdaping and fled; Deguang was specially commended and appointed acting provincial commander of Anyi garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to storm the riverside rebel nest, killing more than two thousand; He Er abandoned Shangdaping and fled; Deguang was specially rewarded and appointed acting commander of the Anyi garrison.

sentences.zh: 五年，署貴州提督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as acting provincial commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1866 he served as acting provincial commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 攻克永寧，解安順圍。

translations.literal: He captured Yongning and lifted the siege of Anshun.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yongning and relieved the siege of Anshun.

sentences.zh: 六年，援定番，乘雷雨破賊，斬賊首許八十等，平花山賊屯，拔底季賊巢，晉號博奇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went to aid Dingfan, took advantage of thunder and rain to break the rebels, beheaded the rebel chiefs Xu Baishi and others, pacified the rebel strongholds at Huashan, uprooted the rebel nest at Diji, and was advanced in title to Boqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he went to relieve Dingfan, used a thunderstorm to smash the rebels, killed the chiefs Xu Baishi and others, cleared the camps at Huashan, uprooted the nest at Diji, and received the advanced title Boqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 尋勦賊安平蘆荻哨，深入賊伏，中槍陣亡。

translations.literal: Soon afterward while suppressing rebels at Anping Ludi Shao he penetrated deep into a rebel ambush, was struck by gunfire, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, while suppressing rebels at Anping Ludi Shao, he pushed deep into an ambush, was shot, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔依提督陣亡賜卹，贈太子太保，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，諡剛節，建專祠。

translations.literal: An edict granted condolence according to the precedent for a provincial commander killed in battle, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Commandant of the Cloud Cavalry, posthumously named him Gangjie, and ordered a special shrine built.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted him the honors due a provincial commander killed in battle, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, gave his family a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry with an additional Commandant of the Cloud Cavalry, named him Gangjie, and ordered a shrine built in his memory.

sentences.zh: 遺腹生子秉鈞，襲世職，復姓張氏。

translations.literal: A posthumous son Bingjun was born; he inherited the hereditary rank and restored the surname Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous son, Bingjun, was born; he inherited the hereditary office and restored the Zhang surname.

sentences.zh: 張文德，湖南鳳凰廳人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wende was a native of Fenghuang Subprefecture in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wende came from Fenghuang Subprefecture in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 幼育於文氏，從姓文，名龍德。

translations.literal: Raised in youth by the Wen family, he took the surname Wen and the given name Longde.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from childhood by the Wen family, he took the surname Wen and the name Longde.

sentences.zh: 入行伍，隸鎮筸營。

translations.literal: He entered the ranks and was attached to the Zheng'gan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He entered military service and was assigned to the Zheng'gan garrison.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，從剿江寧、廬州，敘把總。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he followed in suppressing Jiangning and Luzhou and was recorded as platoon leader.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he campaigned at Jiangning and Luzhou and was recorded as platoon leader.

sentences.zh: 六年，從提督和春攻三河賊壘不下，文德請獨身持檄諭賊降，投誠者相繼至，遂克三河。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, following Grand Secretary He Chun in attacking the rebel fort at Sanhe without success, Wende asked to go alone bearing a proclamation to persuade the rebels to surrender; those submitting in allegiance came in succession, and Sanhe was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: In 1856, when Grand Secretary He Chun's assault on the rebel fort at Sanhe stalled, Wende volunteered to go in alone with a surrender proclamation; defectors came over one after another, and Sanhe fell.

sentences.zh: 七年，從復鎮江，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in the recovery of Zhenjiang and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he took part in the recovery of Zhenjiang and was promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，從援福建，下浦城、松溪、政和、崇安，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed in aiding Fujian, captured Pucheng, Songxi, Zhenghe, and Chong'an, and was awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1858 he went to aid Fujian, took Pucheng, Songxi, Zhenghe, and Chong'an, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 九年，敘援浙江功，晉游擊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his merit in aiding Zhejiang was recorded and he was advanced to regimental commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1859 his service in aiding Zhejiang was recognized and he was promoted to regimental commander.

sentences.zh: 十年，從張國樑解鎮江圍，援賊復至，文德扼水柵七晝夜，賊引去，擢副將。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed Zhang Guoliang in lifting the siege of Zhenjiang; when relief rebels returned, Wende held the water palisade for seven days and nights and the rebels withdrew; he was promoted to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860 he served under Zhang Guoliang in relieving Zhenjiang; when rebel reinforcements returned, Wende held the water palisade for seven days and nights until they withdrew, and he was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 自是從將軍巴棟阿、提督馮子材守鎮江。

translations.literal: From then on he followed General Badong'a and provincial commander Feng Zicai in defending Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he defended Zhenjiang under General Badong'a and provincial commander Feng Zicai.

sentences.zh: 十一年，補廣東羅定協副將。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed deputy commander of the Luoding garrison in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 he was appointed deputy commander of the Luoding garrison in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，賊屢攻鎮江，皆擊退。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi rebels repeatedly attacked Zhenjiang and were each time driven back.
translations.idiomatic: In 1862 the rebels attacked Zhenjiang again and again, and each time he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 馮子材奏言：「文德力挫賊鋒，重圍疊解，實為特出之材。」

translations.literal: Feng Zicai memorialized: "Wende forcefully blunted the rebels' spearhead, lifted siege after siege, and is truly an outstanding talent."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicai memorialized: "Wende has repeatedly broken the rebel assault, lifted one siege after another, and is plainly a man of exceptional ability."

sentences.zh: 授貴州鎮遠鎮總兵，賜號翼勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was appointed provincial commander of Zhenyuan garrison in Guizhou and granted the title Yiyong Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed provincial commander of the Zhenyuan garrison in Guizhou and given the title Yiyong Baturu.

sentences.zh: 文德以生父年七十無子，養父文氏有二子，陳請復姓，更名文德。

translations.literal: Because his biological father at seventy had no son while his adoptive Wen family had two sons, Longde petitioned to restore his original surname and changed his name to Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Raised as Wen Longde, he petitioned to restore the Zhang surname and take the name Wende because his biological father at seventy had no son while his adoptive Wen family already had two.

sentences.zh: 二年，連破賊牧馬口、薛村，克柏林村賊壘，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the second year he repeatedly defeated rebels at Mumakou and Xue Village, captured the rebel fort at Bolin Village, and was given the rank of provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1863 he routed the rebels at Mumakou and Xue Village, stormed the fort at Bolin Village, and received provincial commander rank.

sentences.zh: 賊由東路來犯，文德禦諸駭溪、諫壁，腹中砲，腸出，裹創而戰，援軍至，賊乃退；

translations.literal: Rebels came to attack from the eastern route; Wende defended them at Haixi and Jianbi, was struck in the abdomen by cannon fire with his intestines protruding, bound his wound and continued fighting until relief arrived and the rebels withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: When rebels struck from the east, Wende met them at Haixi and Jianbi; a cannon ball tore open his belly, yet he wrapped the wound and kept fighting until reinforcements came and the enemy withdrew;

sentences.zh: 又破之博洛村，攻丹陽，毀賊壘，擒賊目。

translations.literal: He again defeated them at Boluo Village, attacked Danyang, destroyed rebel forts, and captured rebel officers.
translations.idiomatic: He then defeated them at Boluo Village, attacked Danyang, destroyed their forts, and took several rebel officers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 三年，克白堍鎮及寶堰，賊黨紛紛來降。

translations.literal: In the third year he captured Baichu Town and Baoyan, and rebel followers came over in succession to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 he took Baichu Town and Baoyan, and rebel bands surrendered in large numbers.

sentences.zh: 會鮑超攻丹陽，招賊酋蔣鑑為內應，克其城，斬賊酋陳時永，擒賴桂芳，以提督記名。

translations.literal: When Bao Chao attacked Danyang, he recruited the rebel chieftain Jiang Jian as an inside collaborator; the city was taken, the rebel chieftain Chen Shiyong was beheaded, Lai Guifang was captured, and Wende was recorded as provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao Chao besieged Danyang with the rebel chief Jiang Jian as an inside contact, the city fell; rebel chief Chen Shiyong was killed, Lai Guifang was captured, and Wende was entered on the rolls as provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 江南平，予一品封典，命赴鎮遠鎮本任。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, he was granted first-rank enfeoffment honors and ordered to proceed to his substantive post at Zhenyuan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified, he received first-rank enfeoffment honors and was ordered to take up his post at the Zhenyuan garrison.

sentences.zh: 四年，總督勞崇光令募楚勇規荔波、獨山。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Governor-General Luo Chongguang ordered him to recruit Chu braves to plan operations against Libo and Dushan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1865 Governor-General Luo Chongguang ordered him to raise Hunan braves for operations toward Libo and Dushan.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，解職。

translations.literal: Upon entering mourning for his father, he resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 六年，署貴州提督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as acting provincial commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867 he served as acting provincial commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，克開州，破鼎照山賊砦，克龍里、貴定，斬賊酋潘名桀，餘賊多降，被珍賚。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he captured Kaizhou, broke the rebel stockade at Mount Dingzhao, took Longli and Guiding, beheaded the rebel chieftain Pan Mingjie, most of the remaining rebels surrendered, and he received special rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1868 he took Kaizhou, stormed the stockade on Mount Dingzhao, recovered Longli and Guiding, killed the rebel chief Pan Mingjie, accepted the surrender of most of the rest, and received special honors from the court.

sentences.zh: 進攻平越，擒金大五，連克麻哈、都勻，賜黃馬褂，晉號達桑阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Pingyue, captured Jin Dawu, captured Maha and Duyun in succession, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and was advanced in title to Dasang'a Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack on Pingyue, captured Jin Dawu, took Maha and Duyun in succession, received the yellow riding jacket, and was given the advanced title Dasang'a Baturu.

sentences.zh: 請假歸葬親，文德既去，賊复熾。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return and bury his parent; once Wende had gone, the rebels again grew fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave to bury his parent at home, and once Wende was gone the rebels flared up again.

sentences.zh: 八年，回貴州，以糧匱軍潰，都勻复陷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned to Guizhou; because supplies were exhausted the army collapsed, and Duyun fell again.
translations.idiomatic: In 1869 he returned to Guizhou, but shortages broke his army and Duyun was lost again.

sentences.zh: 詔原之，免議，署古州鎮。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him, exempted him from censure, and appointed him acting commander of Guzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The throne pardoned him, waived disciplinary action, and restored him as acting commander of the Guzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 十年，授威寧鎮總兵，督軍剿古州苗。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed provincial commander of Weining garrison and directed the army in suppressing the Miao at Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1871 he was made provincial commander of the Weining garrison and led the campaign against the Guzhou Miao.

sentences.zh: 由九甲、五台山、扁擔山及古州、丹江分路雕剿，年餘，苗渠先後伏誅。

translations.literal: From Jiujia, Mount Wutai, Mount Biandan, and Guzhou and Danjiang he divided his forces for search-and-destroy operations; after more than a year the Miao ringleaders were executed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: He split his forces along routes through Jiujia, Mount Wutai, Mount Biandan, Guzhou, and Danjiang; after more than a year the Miao chiefs were hunted down and executed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，全黔肅清，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year all Guizhou was pacified, and he was given a hereditary rank of Commandant of the Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1874, when all Guizhou was pacified, he received a hereditary Commandant of the Cloud Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，加頭品頂帶，擢貴州提督，剿平黎平侗匪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was given the first-rank official's hat button, promoted to provincial commander of Guizhou, and suppressed the Dong bandits of Liping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1875 he received the first-rank hat button, was promoted to provincial commander of Guizhou, and pacified the Dong bandits of Liping.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，賜卹，貴陽建專祠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; condolence was granted and a special shrine was built at Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he died; the court granted condolence honors and ordered a shrine built for him at Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：江忠源諸弟並從治軍，忠義最為傑出，將大用而早沒，時論惜之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Jiang Zhongyuan's younger brothers all followed him in managing the army; Zhongyi was the most outstanding in loyalty and righteousness; he was about to be greatly employed when he died early, and public opinion regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Jiang Zhongyuan's brothers all took up arms under him, and Zhongyi stood out for loyalty and courage; he was on the verge of high appointment when he died young, to the regret of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 週寬世為李續賓所倚，無役不從，及自將亦未著奇績。

translations.literal: Zhou Kuanshi was relied upon by Li Xubin and did not fail to follow in any campaign, yet when he commanded in his own right he also did not achieve remarkable merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Kuanshi was a man Li Xubin trusted and he followed him in every campaign, but when he commanded on his own he never won any striking success.

sentences.zh: 石清吉、餘際昌、陳大富、林文察、趙德光等，皆久歷行間，以死勤事。

translations.literal: Shi Qingji, Yu Jichang, Chen Dafu, Lin Wencha, Zhao Deguang, and others all long served in the field and died in diligent performance of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qingji, Yu Jichang, Chen Dafu, Lin Wencha, Zhao Deguang, and others all spent long years in the field and died in the service of the state.

sentences.zh: 張文德佐馮子材守鎮江，功最著，底定黔疆，與有勞焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Wende assisted Feng Zicai in defending Zhenjiang with the most outstanding merit, pacified the Guizhou frontier, and shared in the labor of that achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wende aided Feng Zicai in the defense of Zhenjiang with the greatest distinction, helped pacify Guizhou, and had a large share in that accomplishment.
